title: Segmented GPU nodegroups Terraform module with dual-autoscaler fallback and safe upgrade hooks
creator: Evelyn Chen
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that provisions segmented GPU nodegroups in Private (VPC) deployments, supports both Karpenter and ASG-based autoscaling, and implements robust health checks and upgrade-safe lifecycle hooks. The module should enable: workload-segmented pools (latency-critical vs batch), per-pool instance type preferences (on-demand, spot mix), automated graceful draining with driver/firmware upgrade orchestration, and an explicit policy that allows Karpenter to provision and fallback to ASG when provisioning fails or constrained.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes a clear public interface: pool_name, instance_types, spot_capacity_percentage, scaling_strategy (karpenter | asg | hybrid), max_unavailable, upgrade_strategy (rolling | surge), health_check_probe config
Karpenter provisioner can be created by the module and will automatically prefer spot instances while ASG acts as a capacity fallback; both are optional and configurable
Node lifecycle: cordon -> drain -> wait for application liveliness checks -> uninstall GPU driver DaemonSet upgrade -> uncordon. Hooks configurable via module inputs
CI pipeline runs Terraform plan/apply in a dry environment and a teardown; resulting cluster demonstrates safe upgrade with max_unavailable respected
Module includes unit-level examples and a 'canary' provisioning workspace used by infra team before production rollout
Comprehensive docs and recommended RBAC for private control plane and KMS secret usage are included
Health checks: kubelet readiness + nvidia-smi smoke check executed by node-level probe must pass before node rejoins pool
Automated rollback: if >X% of nodes fail healthchecks during upgrade, trigger a pause and surface diagnostic artifacts in console and CI logs
plan: Phase 1: Design public inputs, create skeleton module, and write example for single-pool Karpenter. Phase 2: Add ASG fallback, spot/ondemand mixing, and healthcheck hooks; iterate with teardown tests. Phase 3: Driver upgrade orchestration (DaemonSet + lifecycle hook) and canary run in staging clusters. Phase 4: Docs, runbook, and rollout with feature-flagged production enablement.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: embedding Karpenter provisioner in module gives convenience but risks coupling to cluster-level provisioner policies. Decided to provide an 'opt-in' provisioner resource and clear docs on scope/permissions so platform teams can opt to manage their own provisioners. For driver upgrades, we prefer a DaemonSet-based upgrade with node cordon/drain rather than unmanaged ssh-based flows to keep modules cloud-agnostic.

2026-02-14 - Jordan Miles: Spike results: Karpenter provisioning in staging times out when spot capacity is low; we validated an ASG fallback works by creating synthetic ASG pools. Need to wire proper IAM for Karpenter to check ASG capacity and tag-based fallback policy.

2026-02-18 - SRE reviewer (Miguel Torres): Reviewed healthcheck design; recommended adding a secondary probe that uses 'nvidia-smi --query-gpu' to detect GPU driver deadlocks. Also requested explicit metrics emission (node_upgrade_status gauge) to console dashboard.

2026-02-20 - Security review (Aisha Patel): Flagged that module's default KMS key must not be public; added module input for kms_key_arn and docs to set least-privilege policies. Also required an optional security_review_required flag for releases.

2026-02-25 - Jordan Miles: Implemented draining helper script as Kubernetes Job template invoked by null_resource local-exec during upgrades for ease of testing. Will replace with operator-backed flow in next iteration.

2026-02-28 - Evelyn Chen: Ran a staged canary upgrade in staging-2; observed two nodes fail GPU readiness after driver update. Rollback threshold triggered and upgrade paused as expected. Logs attached to PR #4821 show nvidia-smi timeout; we will add pre-pull of driver binaries and longer post-install readiness timeout as mitigation. Moving ticket to In Progress for follow-up fixes.
